This is a small but very beautiful waterfall. It is not far from the road, less than 15 minutes walk, but it is courteous to ask someone at the Hakmatek Cooperative location if you can take a look. They will most likely ask the local kids to show you, and this is part of the fun as they lead the way. The walk is nice but there is one kind of steep slope and some rocks to climb over.
The kids asked for money, so I gave $10 to the senior gentleman at the Hakmatek site as a tip for their efforts, which seemed appreciated. The Hakmatek Cooperative was not operating when I visited in April 2022.

reviews.text: Between Letefoho and Atsabe is the highest waterfall in Timor-Leste, with a fall of around 200m. It forms part of a minor tributary of the Loes River, the largest river system in the country. It is particularly impressive in the wet season, though the roads to reach it may be impassable then… Allow at least an hour to walk to the base and return from the main road, with decent footwear recommended plus a local guide as the way isn’t obvious.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: Probably the most spectacular waterfall in Timor-Leste, though some effort is required to reach it. Access is off the main road about 45 minutes south of Maubisse, look out for the brown tourism site sign. Allow at least an hour to walk to and from the waterfall along a steep 1.3km path. The path is generally decent, with some steps, but closer to the falls care needs to be taken as it can be slippery. An enterprising local has built a bamboo bridge to access the waterfall, for which payment is required to cross ($1.50 for Timorese and $2 for malae / foreigners).

reviews.name: S Kai
reviews.text:
アイナロの中心から車で30分程。茶色の看板が道路脇に建っています。看板付近に車を停めるスペースがあり、そこから徒歩で片道1時間程です。道は未舗装部分が多いですが、部分的に階段やコンクリート舗装された箇所もあり歩きやすいです。
道中、道を整備していると名乗る男性から通行料を要求されることがあります。最初2ドルと言われましたが、1ドルでも通してくれました（帰る際にはいなくなってました）。
滝の直前、竹の橋が設置されています。滝付近に住んでいる（自称、土地の所有者）おじいさんが設置したもので、通行料は1人1.5ドルです。橋の無い川沿いの道を進むこともできますが、おじいさんに怒られますので竹の橋を渡ることをオススメします。
雨季明けだったため滝壺には入れませんでしたが、凄まじい水量の滝は圧巻でした。
reviews.textTranslated:
It's about a 30-minute drive from the center of Ainaro. There's a brown sign on the side of the road. There's a parking space near the sign, and it's about an hour's walk from there. While much of the road is unpaved, there are some stairs and concrete sections, making it easy to walk.
Along the way, you might encounter a man claiming to be maintaining the road who will ask for a toll. He initially asked for $2, but was happy to let me through for just $1 (he was gone when I left).
Just before the waterfall, there's a bamboo bridge. It was installed by an old man who lives near the waterfall (and claims to be the landowner), and the toll is $1.50 per person. You can also walk along the river without the bridge, but the old man will scold you, so I recommend crossing the bamboo bridge.
Because it was the end of the rainy season, we couldn't enter the basin, but the sheer volume of water was impressive.

reviews.name: John Dooley
reviews.text:
Beautiful waterfall and a lovely walk to get to it.
The place is not well-signposted but going off the map location it is hard to go wrong. The walk up takes less than 30 minutes, but some parts of the trail are pretty gravelly and slippery. Other parts have concrete steps and more were being laid when I was there, so hopefully soon it will be easier to walk on. Take water, there are no kiosks up there or at least there were not at this time.
If you do not have your own transport, you can hire an angguna "mesak" (independently) from Maubisse or Same. I got one by asking around at the market in Same.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: The best known hot springs in the country were developed by the Portuguese, with a resort complex built around the pools, but fell into disrepair. In 2016 the whole complex was redeveloped, but little maintenance appears to have taken place since. As of 2024 the toilets are completely out of action, and derelict buildings surround the pools. The hot springs produce ~2,000 litres of water per minute. There are three pools, one very hot (up to ~50C), one hot, and one cold. Despite only being 55km from Dili, allow at least 5 hours to get there, along increasingly bad roads that require good off-road skills.

Place where you can relax in a warming pool after such a long off-road trip, one of its kind in the country, famous but road is equally challenging. We did this in a group recently travel from north part of Cailaco Raiheuk driving through the farms/jungle and stop the car at the edge of the river, walk for 2km through warm rivers. It was such a nice trekking, with beautiful surrounding, Uma Lulik, local women waving Tais. The water was so natural, warm on river, and the the pool and a bit hot up there in the taps, locals are very friendly.
Ensure you bring enough foods with you when doing off-roading to this area.
If this Hot Spring can be developed maturely, it can bring more tourist and generates incomes.

reviews.name: Roberto Soares
reviews.text: Marobo hot spring is number one turistical spot in Timor Leste, not only hot spring, the areas around it is full of  culture and traditional stuff such as (Uma lulik) traditional house and (Tebe tebe) traditional dance and many more if you are interested in traditional things

reviews.name: William Smith
reviews.text:
A very worthwhile visit. Make sure you get there early in the day. And take refreshments along.
Road down to the hot springs is being resurfaced, but still very steep!

reviews.name: Pedro Catarino
reviews.text: Natural hot springs with permanent running water ... friendly locals.

reviews.name: Bruce Mumford
reviews.text: It's a long hard ride on a scooter from Balibo but if you have the time the scenery was spectacular on the way. But the road is very bad most of the way. Hot springs was fine. I was alone there.
